title: An object declares the states in which a document and its master-detail lines are closed to change (ADR first)
body:
security#2 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcW9L8Noz9BxEwjwiov

**Feature, ADR first. Maintainer ruling 2026-11-22, option C** (record 7073676422 on #32004; analysed by an isolated contract-tier thread).

**Rule.** An object declares the states in which it and its `master_detail` lines refuse add, edit, remove and move: for example approved, paid, closed. Approval, payment and closing only set the state. A record leaves the closed state only through a sanctioned action that moves it back. The runtime refuses changes to a closed record and its lines at every door, with one loud refusal.

**Why.** Today the platform unlocks a record when its approval is decided, as `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` documents. Apps that need a decided document frozen hand-code it:
- the showcase's paid-invoice guard hooks (#24731);
- a hosted app's edit guards.

Removing a line cannot be guarded without code. Seat ruling 6281609466 on #24684 required "a named producer beyond this showcase" before a declarative state lock; that condition is now met. Mainstream ERP modelling is state-driven immutability, with child rows included.

**The ADR settles:**
- the key's shape on the object;
- the unit (the record plus its master-detail lines, the same unit the pending approval lock already uses);
- exemptions (system writes, the record's own delete) and whether a closed document may be deleted;
- one lock read for both producers (the pending approval lock and the declared closed states).

**Then build cards.** Convert the showcase's paid-invoice hooks to the declaration as the proof.

**Not this card:** the pending-window line lock. It is already on main (#35755), and #36135 lands with it.

Re-check: `git grep -n "the record unlocks" origin/main -- content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx` shows today's decided-state behaviour.
